text:
maya: Customer reports intermittent EOF / truncated stream from /v1/stream when using curl. Happens ~10-20% of attempts. They provided a request-id: req_0a1b2c3d4e and a short server-side log snippet. Can someone advise minimal curl steps to collect a reproducible trace?

support_bot: Created ticket #98765 — please attach curl trace + request-id.

ben: Thanks @maya. First ask: are they behind a corporate proxy or using an SDK? Proxies often mess with HTTP/2 chunking. Also which OS and curl version?

maya: They said macOS 12, curl 7.85, corporate proxy in path. Provided this quick curl they tried:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=test-stream"
```

ben: Ok. That default can use HTTP/2 and buffering. For streaming/SSE we usually recommend: 1) force HTTP/1.1, 2) disable buffering, 3) set Accept and Connection headers, 4) collect --trace-ascii and capture stdout. Ask them to run this exact command and upload the trace:

```
curl -N -v --http1.1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=test-stream" \
  --trace-ascii curl.trace
```

ben: Notes: -N / --no-buffer ensures output is flushed. --http1.1 avoids HTTP/2 middlebox quirks. --trace-ascii will capture request/response bytes and timings we need.

olivia: Also ask them to include an explicit x-request-id header (match the server request-id) so we can correlate in logs, e.g.:

```
-H "x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d4e"
```

olivia: If corporate proxy is present, have them try a direct connection (no proxy) or add `--no-keepalive` / `--raw` to see differences. Some Windows/proxy stacks rewrite chunk boundaries.

maya: The customer can run the above. They also shared a small server fragment: "[2026-02-12T14:22:13Z] req_0a1b2c3d4e: write failed: unexpected EOF after 3.2s" — is that helpful?

ben: Yes. That suggests client-side close. In our past incidents that points to either proxy or client curl version buffering. If the trace shows FIN from client we can confirm. Also ask for network tcpdump if they can (but trace usually enough).

eng-oncall: If they upload curl.trace, we'll grep for the request-id and for any zero-length chunk frames. On the backend we can correlate with internal traces. @ben please include the endpoint and exact query params when you reproduce locally.

ben: I'll try to reproduce through a local proxy (mitmproxy) and without. If I see premature 0-length chunk I'll paste the minimal reproducer here.

olivia: One more tip — if their environment injects TLS ALPN meddling, forcing `--http1.1` often fixes it. If they must use HTTP/2, ask them to run with `--http2-prior-knowledge` and collect traces as well.

maya: I'll send the commands to the customer and ask them to: 1) run the curl with --trace-ascii, 2) include x-request-id header, 3) try direct connection if possible, 4) attach the curl.trace and stdout dump.

support_bot: Request #98765 updated with instructions.

ben: If they can't reproduce with the minimal curl, ask for a short recording of exact curl binary (`curl --version`) and environment vars (`env | egrep -i "proxy|http_proxy|HTTPS_PROXY"`).

maya: Got it. Will follow up once they upload trace. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

eng-oncall: If we get curl.trace, run: `grep -n "req_0a1b2c3d4e" curl.trace` and send matches; we'll correlate with logs and check for client FIN.

maya: Closing loop for now — waiting on customer.
